t: You're standing at the remains of Winchester Palace, a twelfth-century bishop's palace on Clink Street, near Southwark Priory. It was the London townhouse of the Bishops of Winchester, and what survives is a scheduled ancient monument, looked after by English Heritage. Lancelot Andrewes lived here. He served under Elizabeth the First and James the First as Bishop of Chichester, then Ely, then Winchester, and he oversaw the translation of the King James Version of the Bible. That makes this ruined house part of the story of one of English's most famous books.
